correctness.rationale: For a vertex cover \(S\), the zero coordinates of an edge-distance vector are exactly its selected endpoints. Two edges with the same intersection with \(S\) must therefore be \(sx\) and \(sy\) with distinct unselected neighbors of the same selected vertex. In a lollipop, a nonattachment clique vertex cannot have two such neighbors; at the attachment vertex the only possible pair is an omitted clique vertex versus \(p_1\), distinguished by selected \(p_2\); at a path vertex, two omitted path neighbors are distinguished by any selected nonattachment clique vertex. Thus every cover edge-resolves. The two cases \(c\in S\) and \(c\notin S\) give the exact minimum-cover size; standard path-cover structure gives the odd/even counts. An independent exhaustive reconstruction for \(3\le m\le5\), \(2\le\ell\le6\) verified every vertex cover and the basis formulas, as corroboration only.

value.rationale: Lollipop graphs are a standard graph family and dominant edge metric dimension is a recently introduced natural hybrid invariant. The theorem identifies a family-specific mechanism making every vertex cover resolve edges and gives the complete minimum-basis census, not merely one scalar value. This is a natural exact family calculation with reusable structural content.
residual_risks: The same family may appear under the name kite or clique-path coalescence in a non-indexed graph-metric paper.

final_claim: For \(m\ge3\) and \(\ell\ge2\), every vertex cover of the lollipop graph \(L_{m,\ell}\) is an edge metric generator. Therefore \(\operatorname{Ddim}_e(L_{m,\ell})=m-1+\lfloor\ell/2\rfloor\), the dominant edge metric bases are exactly the minimum vertex covers, and their number is \(m-1\) for odd \(\ell=2r+1\) and \((m-1)(r+1)+1\) for even \(\ell=2r\).
scientific_limitations: The same family may appear under the name kite or clique-path coalescence in a non-indexed graph-metric paper.
